bullets.title: NVDA: Jefferies previews Aug 26 print — $95B July rev, $108B Oct guide; Rubin ramp drives 2H27 upside
bullets.body: Jefferies (Blayne Curtis) models NVDA July Q revenue of $95B vs. Street $91.9B, with October guidance of $108B vs. $103.7B consensus. Rubin ramps are the key call: 12% of GPU revenue in F3Q27, climbing to ~40-50% by F4Q27. Cloud revenue is inflecting at MSFT and AMZN, OAI is locked in through 2030, and SPCX has committed to all-NVDA architecture. Wolfe and Opco also flag>$1T cumulative Blackwell/Rubin revenue visibility through CY27, while valuations sit at the lowest since the AI upcycle began (16x CY27E vs. five-year avg 32x).

bullets.title: MRVL: Google deal could imply $120B cumulative revenue through FY33; UBS raises PT to $310
bullets.body: Marvell disclosed an expanded commercial agreement with Google spanning custom silicon attached to the TPU ecosystem (AI inference accelerators, storage/NICs/memory controllers, near-memory compute). A warrant structure — 240 tranches tied to $500M of custom product revenue each — implies up to $120B cumulative revenue (~$18B/yr average) over ~7 years. UBS raises PT from $300 to $310 (30x C2028 EPS of $10.31), and notes no negative read-through to AVGO as MRVL is focused on XPU-attach/disaggregated inference rather than TPU development itself. Custom AI ASIC (XPU) sales expected to double to $4B+ next year, reaching $10B+ by CY28.

bullets.title: CRM: JPM Overweight ahead of F2Q — needs CRPO at +13%+ and subscription reaccel signal
bullets.body: JPM's Samik Chatterjee moved CRM to Overweight. Street expects ~+11% Y/Y subscription revenue growth in F2Q; a beat would boost confidence in 2H FY27 reacceleration. cRPO is guided +13% Y/Y FXN organic; FY27 subscription guidance currently +11% FXN needs +11.5% to support the 2H story. Share count is down ~15% Y/Y from an ASR, so per-share metrics will look materially better. Opco maintains $250 PT on favorable F2Q setup with low expectations and strong Agentforce/Data Cloud adoption.

bullets.title: CRWD: CTO departure adds overhang; needs $20M+ NNARR beat and guide raise to move stock
bullets.body: CRWD CTO Elia Zaitsev is departing to launch an AI-focused cyber venture fund called Cognition, adding a personnel overhang to a stock already up ~100% since the April Mythos launch. JPM notes channel conversations are the most positive in any covered company this quarter, but says the stock needs a 2Q NNARR beat of $20M+ with flow-through to FY guidance to move higher. Identity expected to accelerate; Cloud and Next-Gen SIEM are performing strongly.

bullets.title: ADI: 10th consecutive above-seasonal quarter; second price hike mid-Sept; DC drives visibility to 2027
bullets.body: ADI posted F3Q26 revenue of $4.02B (beat $3.91B est) and EPS $3.45 (beat $3.32), with F4Q26 guidance of $4.30B and EPS $3.86 — both ~7-10% above consensus. A second round of price hikes takes effect September 13, expected to provide mid-single-digit revenue impact with gross margin uplift in FY27. Citi raises FY26/27 EPS 3%/7%, maintaining Buy at $460 PT. AI/DC businesses (~20% of sales) expected to grow from ~$3B in FY26 to ~$5.3B by FY28 (32% CAGR). Seaport Research and Bernstein both upgraded ADI to Buy/Outperform on the print.

bullets.title: MU / memory: SK Hynix ₩40tn buyback expands cash return program; MU unlocks post-Dec 2026 Chips Act
bullets.body: Wolfe notes SK Hynix expanded its buyback from 50% to >50% FCF with quarterly execution rather than post-CY27, and a special dividend and ordinary dividend increase under consideration. GS notes SK Hynix EPS was raised 4%/10%/10% for 2026E/2027E/2028E. MU will unlock incremental cash returns once Chips Act restrictions expire in December 2026. Memory upcycle remains intact on tight inventories, strong KV cache demand, and HBM shortage. NVDA is pushing HBM vendors to exceed JEDEC HBM4 spec to 11 GBPS to stay ahead of AMD MI450; SK Hynix has already hit that mark.

bullets.title: BABA: Q1 Cloud revenue +45% YoY but EPS misses on margin compression and capex surge
bullets.body: BABA reported Q1 revenue of CNY268.95B (in-line) but EPS of CNY8.52 vs. CNY10.14 consensus (miss). AI Cloud revenue accelerated to +45% YoY with 12% EBITA margin. Operating margin declined 8pp YoY to 6% as capex surged 75% YoY to CNY67.68B vs. Tencent's CNY53bn, and FCF turned deeply negative. International eCommerce declined 20% YoY. Quick commerce grew 45%.

bullets.title: DIS: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight with $125 PT; Disney+ path to 20%+ EBIT margins
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW with $125 PT (~15x FY28 EPS of $8.33), noting Disney+ has similar margins on similar revenues to Netflix in 2019 with a path to 20%+ EBIT margins on $30B+ revenues in ~5 years. Parks/Experiences durability supported by $60B capex over 10 years. Content catalysts include Avengers: Doomsday ($1.8B Dec '26), Frozen III ($1.4B Nov '27), and Secret Wars ($2.0B Dec '27). EPS CAGR of 12-13% FY26-30.

bullets.title: FOXA: Wolfe raises PT to $93 on $1B Roku merger synergies; 36.8% upside
bullets.body: Wolfe Research raises FOXA PT to $93 (Outperform) on ~$1B incremental EBITDA from cost and revenue synergies post-Roku merger. Roku data could boost Tubi revenue ~$125M via enhanced ad targeting; Fox's ad sales team could drive ~$300M uplift for Roku; Roku's content hooks could add 1M Fox One subscribers. Pro-forma FOXA trades at 12.1x fully-synergized UFCF and 9.7x EBITDA. SOTP suggests fair value of $105/share.

bullets.title: CHTR: Cox/Liberty deal closes; Charter issues ~46M shares, Cox owns ~26%, expects $500M synergies
bullets.body: Charter completed its acquisition of Cox Communications and Liberty Broadband. Charter issued ~46M shares to Cox Enterprises; Cox now owns ~26% of the combined entity on a fully diluted basis. Net share count decreased ~4.7M from the Liberty transaction. ~$12B of Cox debt remains at Charter subsidiaries. Pro forma net leverage ~3.9x; long-term target 3.50-4.00x. Combined company to be renamed Cox Communications within one year. Charter expects ~$500M annualized cost synergies within three years.

bullets.title: ETSY: BofA and Rosenblatt both initiate Buy; 18-30% upside cited
bullets.body: BofA upgraded ETSY from neutral to Buy, raising PT to $105 from $88 (30% upside from $80.46). Separately, Rosenblatt initiated ETSY at Buy with a $95 PT (18% upside). Pre-market ETSY was trading +2.7%.

bullets.title: NBIS: Upsizes convertible to $5B; proceeds fund data center expansion and GPU procurement
bullets.body: Nebius upsized its convertible note offering from $4.5B to $5.0B: $3.0B of 0.50% 2030 notes at ~$313.46 conversion price (40% premium) and $2.0B of 4.50% 2034 notes at ~$324.65 (45% premium). The company is simultaneously exchanging $800M of existing convertibles for ~15.8M Class A shares. Proceeds fund data center expansion, full-stack AI cloud development, and GPU procurement.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Morgan Stanley reiterates EQIX OW ($1,250 PT) on open-weight AI and interconnection pricing
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates EQIX as top pick with $1,250 PT; open-weight AI model adoption tilts incremental inference demand toward colocation providers. Interconnection pricing is an underappreciated lever; sovereign AI/data residency trends favor EQIX's global distributed footprint. Closed-weight outcomes would skew more to hyperscale-focused DLR, though EQIX participates via xScale. Citi separately supports both EQIX ($1,260 PT) and DLR ($226 PT) after the Applied Digital data center tour.

bullets.title: SPHR: Piper Sandler initiates Overweight at $185 PT on live entertainment strength
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiated Sphere Entertainment (SPHR) at Overweight with a $185 PT (16% upside from $159.79), calling it levered to strong live entertainment ex-sports consumer spending. Vegas market expectations are seen as achievable in '27E with additional upside from venue rollout. MSG Entertainment (MSGE) was initiated at Neutral with an $86 PT, as premium venue valuation at ~15x '27E AOI feels factored in.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Rosenblatt upgrades to Buy with $410 PT; YouTube offering millions for exclusive creator content
bullets.body: Rosenblatt upgraded GOOGL from Neutral to Buy, raising the PT to $410 from $393 (19% upside). Separately, YouTube is offering millions of dollars to popular creators for exclusive upload periods to counter Netflix's talent acquisition strategy. Hedgeye signals GOOGL as Bearish trend; buy range $335, sell $359.

bullets.title: INTC: Razor Lake reportedly shifting to TSMC N2X; may squeeze AMD TSMC server CPU capacity
bullets.body: Rumors indicate Intel's upcoming Razor Lake desktop processor will use TSMC's high-performance N2X (2nm) process. An analyst argues Intel can block AMD from securing additional TSMC server CPU capacity simply by maintaining or increasing its own fab allocation. Samsung is also prioritizing 2nm foundry expansion (SF2P/SF2P+) for mass production next year. TSM CoWoS packaging is full and Samsung has raised foundry prices up to 15%.

bullets.title: LRCX: UBS sees ~40% upside; WFE share rising from 11.5% to >15% by 2027 on NAND and packaging spend
bullets.body: UBS ranks LRCX near the top of its HOLT scorecard (peer rank 98) with CFROI forecast to rise to ~40% next year from ~30%. WFE share is expected to climb from ~11.5% in 2025 to >15% by 2027 driven by NAND upgrades and advanced packaging spending. HOLT market-implied scenario embeds only 10% long-term sales growth vs. consensus of 50% for next year.

bullets.title: FN: Wolfe maintains Outperform at $775 PT; NVDA transceiver business dipped 40-50% Q/Q in June
bullets.body: Wolfe Research maintains Outperform on Fabrinet (FN) at $775 PT (~70% upside). NVIDIA transceiver revenue fell ~40-50% Q/Q in June (estimated ~$125M vs. $211M prior Q), and NVDA is now <10% of accounts receivable. However, purchase obligations surged 123% YoY to $3.15B (58% of NTM COGS), Telecom/DCI and Nokia optical businesses are expanding, and Amazon transceiver wins are ramping. Analyst expects 30%+ revenue and EPS growth for several years.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: 22V Research long compute on firm pricing; warns on data center regulatory headwinds pre-election
bullets.body: 22V Research is long compute through CRWV and NBIS, citing demand outstripping supply with higher contract rates for next-gen compute (Vera Rubin). Pennsylvania Governor signed an executive order removing data centers from Fast Track permitting — the strictest guardrails in the nation — and data center regulation is becoming a primary midterm election issue in OH, GA, PA, and TX. Anthropic IPO (~early October) expected to be larger than the SpaceX IPO and a critical signal for the AI trade.
